short: A song or expression of praise.
note: A celebratory song of praise or thanksgiving; by extension, an enthusiastic tribute. The word comes from Greek hymns associated with Apollo.
Foam or froth, especially on rough water.
A centaur of Greek mythology who gave hospitality to Heracles. In the ancient accounts, opening the centaurs’ shared wine jar brings the other centaurs to his cave.

short: An epithet for Jesus; a reference in Swinburne’s Hymn to Proserpine.
note: A person from Galilee, especially Jesus. Algernon Charles Swinburne’s Hymn to Proserpine addresses the “Galilean” while lamenting the displacement of the ancient pagan gods by Christianity.
Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu in Hindu tradition, who defeats the tyrant Hiranyakashipu.

short: Lines from Macaulay’s The Battle of the Lake Regillus.
note: The verse describes the divine twins Castor and Pollux in Thomas Babington Macaulay’s The Battle of the Lake Regillus, one of the Lays of Ancient Rome.

short: The hunter transformed into a stag in Greek myth.
note: Actaeon, the hunter transformed into a stag and killed by his own hounds. Percy Bysshe Shelley invokes him in stanza 31 of Adonais, his elegy for John Keats.

short: Possibly Sombelenë in Lord Dunsany’s The Book of Wonder.
note: Possibly Sombelenë, the beautiful, long-lived woman in Lord Dunsany’s The Bride of the Man-Horse, collected in The Book of Wonder. Her ancestry joins a god, a centaur, a lion, and a sphinx.

sources.label: Lord Dunsany · The Book of Wonder

short: Pirithous, the mythological companion of Theseus.
note: Pirithous, companion of Theseus in Greek mythology. The two descend to the underworld in an attempt to obtain Persephone as Pirithous’s bride.

short: Erasmus Darwin, the poet; Charles Darwin, the naturalist.
note: Erasmus Darwin (1731–1802) was a physician, naturalist, and poet, the author of The Loves of the Plants. His grandson Charles Darwin was the naturalist associated with the voyage of the Beagle and evolution by natural selection.

sources.label: Erasmus Darwin · The Loves of the Plants

short: A boat driven by a paddle wheel at the rear.
note: A vessel, especially a riverboat, propelled by a large paddle wheel mounted at its stern.

short: Wax used to block the Sirens’ song.
note: In book 12 of Homer’s Odyssey, Odysseus stops his companions’ ears with wax to protect them from the Sirens; he listens while bound to the mast.
